newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Qatar says too early for single Gulf currency.
newsitem.headline: Qatar says too early for single Gulf currency.

text.p: Qatar's central bank governor Abdullah bin Khaled al-Attiyah said on Sunday it was too early for a unified Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) currency.
"Monetary union will pass through stages," he told a Gulf banking conference in Manama, adding that it would come at the last stage of GCC economic integration.

Attiyah suggested a single currency would be premature now because trade between Gulf Arab states was limited and each country's efforts to deal with budget deficits was linked to their individual currencies.

The GCC -- Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, United Arab Emirates, Qatar, Oman and Bahrain -- is a political and economic alliance. It is working to unify economic and monetary policies as part of a plan to set up a regional market.
Excepting Kuwait, Gulf currencies are pegged to the dollar, in which their main export - crude oil - is traded.
